answers.ask: How far is the walk from town to the forest edge - a few seconds, or a real journey?
answers.answer: A few seconds on foot; the forest should begin just beyond the town via the dirt path so the woodcutting loop is immediately playable.

answers.ask: Medieval is stated for the buildings; should the forest read the same storybook way, or more naturalistic?
answers.answer: Use a polished, naturalistic pine forest that complements the medieval town, with appealing stylized Roblox detail rather than an exaggerated storybook look.

scene_prompt: Create a polished 3D Roblox map for a woodcutting game loop. A small medieval-style town center forms the spawn area, clearly separated from a naturalistic pine forest; a dirt path leads from town to the forest edge only a few seconds away on foot. The forest contains at least 20 detailed pine trees distributed across grassy, uneven terrain with rocks and bushes, with each tree grounded naturally and varied slightly in height, width, and rotation. Pine trees have brown textured trunks and layered green branches. Place the visible axe tool and woodcutting interaction space around the trees; keep the town and nearby forest as the complete playable area, with no mines, shops, combat zones, trading spaces, or quest areas.
agent_notes: A gather-and-bank loop with trees shared server-wide is Simulation's extraction family, and nothing else is in scope — the author explicitly excluded trading, shops, combat and quests — so there is no second genre. I took the Mining & Extraction preset for its resource-shared and collectible-nodes, which describe this exactly (a pine forest the whole server draws from on a 30-second respawn, with the wood as the extractable node), but substituted world-open for the preset's world-underground because nothing here goes below the surface, which also keeps the build off P2 and P3; path-circulation replaces the preset's hauling roads since the dirt path is walked, not driven. The town center comes in as settlement-density for the small medieval hamlet plus social-hub for the square players spawn in and return to, with the wording bent to note it has no shops yet, and the explicitly requested uneven ground is terrain-relief, which is what adds tiered. Deciding without a user: town and forest sit on one continuous surface a few seconds apart, so one map and no P4; no building is enterable, so no P3; and the twenty-plus pine trees, tree health, cooldowns, tool animations, UI and DataStore work are recorded here because they are systems rather than layout picks.
